IN RE SQUIRES BINGHAM LTD.

Sir,

With reference to the attached I have called on Mr. Squires as instructed and he states that in future he will send a letter giving full particulars of any firearm received for disposal, he will also deliver a letter and the pistol to this office after the approval of the Police has been received.

At this interview Mr. Squires stated that he had on many occassions approached the Chinese Customs for a huchao to enable him to import ten pistols but has been refused, Mr. Squires implied that had permission be granted by the Customs he would keep same in the Customs Godown until a sale was effected. Deputy Commissioner,

In re Squires, Bingham, Ltd.

I am pleased to comply with your request for an
opinion relative to the above entitled matter. The
facts may be briefly epitomized as follows:
Squires, Bingham, Ltd. have from time to time sold
arms and ammunition. This corporation does not have a
license either from the American authorities or the
Municipal Council to engage in the business of selling
arms and ammunition. Squires, Bingham, Ltd. has from
time to time reported to the Police the sale of pistols
and the persons to whom such pistols are delivered.
The Municipal Council, although it has power under Bye-
law 35 to issue licenses to persons who sell firearms,
other than those used solely for sporting purposes, does
not issue such licenses to anyone whatsoever. The question
for opinion is whether Messrs. Squires, Bingham, Ltd. is
guilty of an offense under American law.
Section 857 of the District of Columbia Code makes it
an offense to engage in or conduct the business of selling,
bartering, hiring or lending weapons without having prev-
iously obtained from the Commissioners of the District of
Columbia a special license authorizing the conduct of such
business by such person. It is doubtful whether or not this
section can be applied to American citizens residing in
China,

致：
副总监，
罪案及特别分支。

关于 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司事宜。

我很高兴就上述标题事项提供您所请求的意见。事实可简要概括如下：
Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司不时出售武器和弹药。该公司既未从美国当局也未从工部局获得从事武器和弹药销售业务的执照。Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司已不时向警方报告手枪的销售情况及接收这些手枪的人员。工部局虽然根据附则第35条有权向出售非仅用于体育目的的枪支的人员颁发执照，但实际上并未向任何人颁发此类执照。需要征求意见的问题是，Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 诸位先生是否违反了美国法律。
《哥伦比亚特区法典》第857条规定，在未事先从哥伦比亚特区专员处获得授权此人开展此类业务的特别执照的情况下，从事或经营出售、易货、出租或出借武器的业务，即构成犯罪。该条款是否适用于居住在中国的美国公民，尚存疑问，

page_data.en:
-2-

In the case of Royal vs. State of Virginia, 29 Law
Ed., at page 735, the Supreme Court of the United States
held that where an applicant for a license has complied
with the necessary procedure and tendered the required
tax, and the licensing authority has refused to issue the
license, such applicant may, without a license, pursue his
business or profession, which is not unlawful in itself
and which he has a constitutional right to prosecute.

The sale of arms and ammunition under American law,
except to minors, is not in itself unlawful.

It appears that it would be no use for Messrs. Squires
Bingham, Ltd. to apply for a license to the Municipal Council
because same would not be granted, as the granting of licen-
ses to sell arms is contrary to the Council's policy.

The opinion is therefore given that Messrs. Squires,
Bingham, Ltd. are not guilty of an offense under American
law.

I have discussed this matter with Dr. Sellett, the
United States District Attorney. Dr. Sellett has inter-
viewed Mr. Squires. I am informed that Mr. Squires told
Dr. Sellett that the Police agreed to be satisfied if he
would report to them any sales of pistols. He contends that
he has complied with this understanding. He further says
that he is willing to cooperate with the police in every
possible way. On looking through the file, it would appear
that Squires, Bingham, Ltd. ha always informed the police
when pistols have been sold, although the information may
have been given tardily. The United States District Attorney
feels that Mr. Squires is acting in good faith; that he is
not in the business of gun-running, smuggling or selling
arms and ammunition in large quantities.

It

在 Royal 诉弗吉尼亚州一案中，《法律汇编》第29卷，第735页，美国最高法院裁定，如果执照申请人已履行必要程序并缴纳规定税款，而发证机关拒绝颁发执照，则该申请人可以在无执照的情况下继续其本身并不违法且其拥有宪法权利去从事的业务或职业。

根据美国法律，除向未成年人出售外，出售武器和弹药本身并不违法。

看来 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 诸位先生向工部局申请执照并无用处，因为执照不会获批，鉴于颁发枪支销售执照违背工部局的政策。

因此，意见认为 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 诸位先生并未违反美国法律。

我已与美国地区检察官 Sellett 博士讨论此事。Sellett 博士已会见 Squires 先生。据告知，Squires 先生告诉 Sellett 博士，警方同意，只要他向警方报告任何手枪销售情况，警方即感满意。他声称自己已遵守这一谅解。他还表示愿意在各方面尽可能与警方合作。查阅档案后，似乎 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司在出售手枪时总是通知警方，尽管信息提供可能有所延迟。美国地区检察官认为 Squires 先生行事诚信；他并未从事军火走私、偷运或大量出售武器和弹药的生意。

Any person or persons who shall, within the District of
Columbia, sell, barter, hire, lend, or give to any minor under

任何人在未事先从哥伦比亚特区专员处获得授权此人开展此类业务的特别执照的情况下，不得参与或经营出售、易货、出租、出借或赠送任何前述种类的武器的业务。特此授权上述专员在申请人向其提交由经其批准的担保人担保的保证金后，无偿颁发此类执照，保证金金额由其确定，以美国为受益人，条件是该申请人遵守本节的所有规定。一旦违反该条件，美国将为自身利益对该保证金提起诉讼，且上述专员可撤销该执照。任何从事上述业务的人

P.A. (C. B.)

Sir,

On the 14/5/31 a Mr. Lee representing the
Shanghai Commercial & Savings Bank Ltd. came to this office
and requested information as to the procedure necessary
to enable him to change two pistols carried by C.P.W. at
present armed with Police weapons, who are employed at the
North Szechuen Road branch.

On being asked re the source of supply of the
pistols, he stated that same had been purchased from Messrs.
Squires, Bingham Ltd, one being a Bayard, the other a
Remington.

As the arming of C.P.W. does not come under
this Section I referred Mr. Lee to Assistant Commissioner
(Chinese) for information.

I communicated with Supt Liang of A.C. (C) office
and he stated that he had instructed Mr. Lee to produce the
pistols.

This morning Mr. Lee in company with Mr. Squires
came to this office and Mr. Squires produced the pistols
together with the attached letter.*

We have trace of the Remington, this was
previously licenced under No.680 in the name of H. Gulick
(since deceased) and bears S.M.P. registration No. Y.746.

The other pistol has not been recorded in this
office and according to Mr. Squires was the property of
J. B. Spunt 1363 Rue Lafayette.

（批：Pistols not seen at H.Q. but supposed to be in possession of Bank Men）
（批：* Letter handed over to A.C.(C) for record. A Young 15/5）

助理总监（中央捕房）

先生：

1931年5月14日，代表上海商业储蓄银行有限公司的 Lee 先生来到本办公室，询问必要的程序，以便更换目前由在北四川路分行任职的两名武装巡捕（C.P.W.）所携带的两支手枪，这些巡捕目前配备的是警用武器。

当被问及手枪来源时，他表示这些手枪购自 Squires, Bingham Ltd. 公司，一支为 Bayard 牌，另一支为 Remington 牌。

由于武装巡捕的配枪事宜不属于本科室管辖范围，我将 Lee 先生引荐至助理总监（华务）处获取信息。

我与助理总监（华务）办公室的 Liang 巡官进行了沟通，他表示已指示 Lee 先生出示手枪。

今天上午，Lee 先生与 Squires 先生一同来到本办公室，Squires 先生出示了手枪及随附信函。*

我们有 Remington 手枪的记录，该枪此前以 H. Gulick（已故）的名义注册，执照号为680号，并带有上海公共租界警务处注册号 Y.746。

另一支手枪在本办公室无记录，据 Squires 先生称，该枪属于住在拉斐特路1363号的 J. B. Spunt。

（批注：总部未见手枪，但推测在银行人员手中）

Sir,
Reference attached, as instructed, I visited
Mr. Squires re his memo of 25th, November 1930 and he stated
that he had no desire whatever to evade any instructions
which the Police may issue.
In this case he states that the pistol was
imported under Huchao obtained by Mr. Perputuo and as this
person was an employee of the S.M.C. he thought that it
would be quite in order.
He also states that he gave Mr. Perputuo the
attached letter and the pistol on the understanding that
same was to be delivered to this office.
I have informed Mr. Squires of the procedure
necessary and he states that in future all arms for disposal
will be sent to this department by his firm direct.
I have interviewed Mr. Perputuo and directed
him to regain possession of the pistol in question and
return same to this office which he states he will do.

Sir,
Mr. Bryan, M.A., was consulted in this matter and states
that it is inadvisable to proceed against Mr. Squires through
the Bye Laws, as it is still a moot point whether the Land
Regulations and Bye Laws apply to American Citizens.
A bill is before the Senate, but has not yet been passed
and various difficult situations might arise if the applicability
was contested.
Under the Code of Laws for the District of Columbia, Sect.
857, a licence is necessary before arms can be sold by an Ameri-
can Citizen, but whether such application for a licence should
be made direct or through the U. S. Consul or even to the S.M.C.
is not definitely known.
Again the S.M.C. would perhaps refuse such an application
on the grounds of creating a precedent.
Mr. Bryan suggests that before any action is contemplated,
Mr. Squires should be definitely warned that in the event of
further sale, he will be proceeded against.
I respectfully suggest that certain conditions as mentioned
in my previous report be made clear to Mr. Squires by some person
in authority. From the attitude of Mr. Squires when interviewed,
he appears to be genuine and willing to conform with any such
requirements or regulations as laid down.

D. S. I. Robinson

He stated that he had kept no records of these sales, either

make of pistol.
Further that he only recollects selling one pistol to an
Army Officer some two years ago. He assured me that he has not

SOLDIER CHARGED
WITH FRAUD

Alleged to Have Obtained Ring,
Saxophone, Pistol With Aid
of Forged Documents

DECISION TO BE GIVEN
TO-DAY

Pte. David Irvine Murie, of the
R.A.M.C., appeared on remand at
H. M. Police Court yesterday on
three charges of uttering forged
documents with intent to cheat and
defraud. Seven other charges of
obtaining goods by false pretences
were held in abeyance pending the
decision of the Registrar (Mr. C. H.
Haines) regarding an application for
his committal for trial at H. M.
Supreme Court made by the As-
sistant Municipal Advocate, Mr.
R. S. W. Winter.

The three charges proceeded with
yesterday concerned a diamond ring
supplied by Mr. Carl Mondenach, 177
Bubbling Well Road, on July 4, a
pistol and ammunition handed to the
accused by Messrs. Squires, Bing-
ham, Ltd., 52 Nanking Road, on
July 8; and a saxophone provided by
Messrs. S. Moutrie & Co., Ltd., on
July 12.

It was alleged that the accused
obtained possession of these articles
by representing himself to be the
batman of "Lieut. Murie," "Capt.
Murie" in person, and the servant of
fictitious or former officers in the
local Defence Force.

Decision To-day

The Registrar, who was accom-
panied on the bench during part of
the proceedings by his Lordship
Judge G. W. King, said that he
would give his decision regarding
Mr. Winter's application at 10 a.m.
to-day.

Mr. Eric Brooks, salesman of
Messrs. S. Moutrie & Co., Ltd., said
that on July 12 his firm received a
telephone message purporting to be
from "Lieut. Murie" of the R.A.M.C.,
in consequence of which the accused
was given a saxophone against an
I.O.U. signed by "Lieut. Murie" and
guaranteed by a "Major Rowlette."
It had since been found that neither
of these men was in Shanghai.

Lieut. Herbert Whitfield Daukes, of
the R.A.M.C., said that he knew a
Major Rowlette of the R.A.M.C.,
who had left Shanghai at about the
end of last February and was now
in Hongkong. The signature on the
I.O.U. given to Messrs. Moutrie,
while not unlike that of Major Row-
lette was not his. There was no
"Lieut. Murie" here.

Mr. R. W. Squires said that he
was the proprietor of Messrs. Squir-
es, Bingham, Ltd., 52 Nanking Road.
On July 8 the accused examined
some pistols and ammunition and
selected a pistol which he said was
for "Lieut. G. W. M. Smith" of the
R.A.M.C., who was leaving immedi-
ately for Tientsin. He took this
pistol and some ammunition away
at 3 p.m. after giving an I.O.U. and
an order signed by "Lieut. Smith."
In answer to the Court, Mr. Squires
said he was not suspicious of the
accused at the time as it was usual
for officers to purchase pistols from
him in this way.

Poor Imitation

Capt. Alexander Graham, of the
R.A.O.C., then gave evidence to the
effect that a "Lieut. Smith" had
been stationed in Shanghai until
July 8, when he left for Tientsin.
He was well acquainted with this
Lieut. Smith's handwriting. The
I.O.U. and order purporting to have
been written by him and given to
Messrs. Squires, Bingham were
"most certainly" not in his hand-
writing, but were a very poor imita-
tion.

Mr. Carl Mondenach said that he
was the proprietor of a jewellery
shop at 177 Bubbling Well Road. On
July 4 in consequence of a telephone
message received from "Capt. Murie"
of the R.A.M.C., he handed the ac-
cused two necklaces and one chain
on approval. These were returned
by the accused with the statement
that "Capt. Murie" did not consider
them good enough and would like in-
stead to buy some diamond rings.
Two diamond rings, one valued at
$600 and the other at $300, were
given to him against his receipt.
The ring valued at $300 had been
returned; but the other was missing.
The accused said that "Capt. Murie"
would pay for this ring on July 28.
When inquiries were made at the
Military Hospital for this "Capt.
Murie" the accused said that he was
very sick but that he (the accused)
had been authorized to arrange a
guarantee on "Capt. Murie's" behalf
with a "higher up" officer. This
"guarantee" was forthcoming. It
was signed by "Capt. Murie" and
by a "Major J. Rowlette."

Lieut. Daukes, recalled, said that
no officer answering to either of
these names was stationed in Shang-
hai.

士兵被控欺诈

据称借助伪造文件获取戒指、萨克斯管和手枪

今日将作出裁决

皇家陆军医疗团（R.A.M.C.）二等兵戴维·欧文·默里（David Irvine Murie）昨日在英王陛下警察法庭还押候审，面临三项使用伪造文件意图欺骗和诈骗的指控。另有七项以虚假借口获取货物的指控暂予搁置，待书记官（C. H. Haines 先生）就助理市政检察官 R. S. W. Winter 先生提出的将其移送英王陛下最高法院受审的申请作出决定后再行处理。

昨日审理的三项指控涉及：7月4日由南京路177号 Carl Mondenach 先生提供的一枚钻戒；7月8日由南京路52号 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司交给被告的一把手枪及弹药；以及7月12日由 S. Moutrie & Co., Ltd. 公司提供的一支萨克斯管。

据称，被告通过自称是“默里中尉”的勤务兵、“默里上尉”本人，以及当地防卫部队中虚构或前任军官的仆人，从而占有了这些物品。

今日裁决

书记官在部分审讯过程中由金法官（Judge G. W. King）阁下陪同出庭，他表示将于今日上午10时就 Winter 先生的申请作出裁决。

S. Moutrie & Co., Ltd. 公司的推销员 Eric Brooks 先生称，7月12日，他的公司收到一通声称来自皇家陆军医疗团“默里中尉”的电话留言，因此公司向被告提供了一支萨克斯管，换取了一张由“默里中尉”签署并由一位“罗莱特少校（Major Rowlette）”担保的欠条。事后发现，这两人均不在上海。

皇家陆军医疗团的赫伯特·惠特菲尔德·多克斯（Herbert Whitfield Daukes）中尉称，他认识皇家陆军医疗团的一位罗莱特少校，该少校已于去年二月底左右离开上海，现居香港。交给 Moutrie 公司的欠条上的签名虽然与罗莱特少校的签名不无相似之处，但并非其亲笔。此处并无“默里中尉”此人。

R. W. Squires 先生称，他是南京路52号 Squires, Bingham, Ltd. 公司的业主。7月8日，被告查看了一些手枪和弹药，并挑选了一把手枪，称这是给即将立即前往天津的皇家陆军医疗团“G. W. M. 史密斯中尉”的。他在下午3点留下了一张由“史密斯中尉”签署的欠条和订单后，取走了这把手枪和一些弹药。回答法庭提问时，Squires 先生表示当时并未怀疑被告，因为军官通常以这种方式从他这里购买手枪。

拙劣的模仿

随后，皇家陆军军械团（R.A.O.C.）的亚历山大·格雷厄姆（Alexander Graham）上尉作证称，一位“史密斯中尉”一直驻守在上海，直到7月8日前往天津。他非常熟悉这位史密斯中尉的笔迹。声称由他书写并交给 Squires, Bingham 公司的欠条和订单“肯定”不是他的笔迹，而是一种非常拙劣的模仿。

Carl Mondenach 先生称，他是南京路177号一家珠宝店的店主。7月4日，因收到来自皇家陆军医疗团“默里上尉”的电话留言，他将两条项链和一条链子交给被告试看。被告将这些物品退回，并称“默里上尉”认为它们不够好，想改买一些钻戒。于是，凭被告出具的收据，向他提供了两枚钻戒，一枚价值600元，另一枚价值300元。价值300元的戒指已被退回；但另一枚下落不明。被告称，“默里上尉”将于7月28日支付这枚戒指的款项。当向军医院查询这位“默里上尉”时，被告称他病得很重，但他（被告）已获授权代表“默里上尉”与一位“上级”军官安排担保。这份“担保”随后出具。它由“默里上尉”和一位“J. 罗莱特少校（Major J. Rowlette）”签署。

多克斯中尉再次出庭作证称，上海没有驻防符合这两个名字的任何军官。

August 6th., 1930.

P.A. (C. & S.B.).

Sir,

On August 5th I received the attached letter from Messrs Squires Bingham Ltd., notifying the Police of the sale of a Colt auto. pistol which was formerly the property of the late Mr. Lyman.

The purchase was made on July 31st by one Yao Zung residing at 31 Medhurst Road who called at this office this morning with the weapon and made application for a licence to carry same.

Yao Zung a youth of barely 21 is a student at St. John's University. He already has a bodyguard permit for two Chinese attendants and in view of his age and the fact that he is still at school I do not think it advisable to grant him permission to carry himself.

With regard to the sale of the pistol I beg to draw your attention to the fact that the Police were not notified of the transaction until after the sale had been completed. This is not in keeping with the usual procedure adopted by Squires Bingham Ltd. and I suggest they be reminded that they are not licensed to sell firearms, and that transactions of this nature are permitted expressly by the C. of P. after the approval of the prospective purchaser.

D. S. I.

July 25th 30

Commissioner of Police
Shanghai
Sir;

In reply to your letter in reference to the sale
of one pistol to Pvt Murie, who posed as the representative
of a British Army Officer we wish to offer the following
explanation.
We have been in business for many years in Shanghai
selling sporting goods of all kinds including sporting guns
and ammunition under Municipal regulations.
Last year we took an order an American citizen of
Shanghai for one Colt pistol to be imported under a permit
issued by the Chinese Govt. When it was received and ready
for delivery Mr Smith asked the Police for a permit to posess
a d we reported the sale to the C.I.D Mr Sharman.
We discussed the matter with him very fully and he
advised us that it would be satisfactory to the Police if
we should report each sale or importation of any gun for an
individual and this we have done in every case.
The C.I.D file will no doubt contain our letters
regarding each sale in detail as to where the gun was
obtained and to whom sold. The gun not being delivered
before permit was obtained or the gun being placed in the
care of the Police until permit was issued.
In this sale in question we were under the impression
that Army Officers were not required to obtain permits from
the Police and so , as we were certain that the sale was for
an Officer that we did not think it would be necessary to
report it, as done with Civilians.
We have no intention or desire to evade any regulations
and we were carefull to report each sale and all the business
done, which is very small, has been done under direct supervision
of the Police and under knowledge of the C.I.D Dept .
Trusting that this will be satisfactory.

Respectfully
Squires Bingham Co
R. M. Squires

1930年7月25日

上海警务处长
先生；

就阁下关于向冒充英国军官代表的二等兵默里出售一把手枪一事去信询问，谨作如下解释。
我们在上海经营多年，根据工部局规章，销售各类体育用品，包括运动枪支和弹药。
去年，我们接受了一位上海美国公民的订单，订购一把柯尔特手枪，依据中国政府颁发的许可证进口。当货物收到并准备交付时，Smith 先生向警方申请持有许可证，并向刑事侦缉处的 Sharman 先生报告了此次销售。
我们就此事与他进行了充分讨论，他建议如果我们报告每一笔个人枪支的销售或进口，警方将会满意，我们在每一起案件中都这样做了。
刑事侦缉处档案中无疑存有我们关于每笔销售的详细信件，说明枪支来源及销售对象。在获得许可证之前，枪支不予交付，或者在颁发许可证之前将枪支交由警方保管。
在本次有争议的销售中，我们以为军官无需从警方获得许可证，因此，既然我们确信购买者是军官，我们认为没有必要像对待平民那样进行报告。
我们无意也无意愿规避任何规章，我们谨慎地报告了每一笔销售，所有业务量很小，均在警方的直接监督和刑事侦缉处的知情下进行。
相信此举能令阁下满意。

此致
敬礼
Squires Bingham 公司
R. M. Squires

when filled may be used for in Canton.

Commerce, 3 Canton Road. He is a native of Szechuen and his
position with the U.S. Department of Commerce allows him to
encourage Chinese, who make enquiries for goods, to buy those

由 D. S. Telfer 撰写，由督察 W.W.Kay 转呈。

先生，

1926年8月9日至11日期间，一名名为黄漢忠 (Wong Han Tsong) 的华人接触了斯奎尔斯·宾厄姆公司的业主 J.W. Baldwin 先生，询问发往广州的50,000发和100,000发空猎枪子弹（类型见附件）的报价。该华人承认他是为一位本地朋友进行询价，该朋友可以很容易地获得一张广州海关护照 (Huchow) 以便进口这些物品。然而，Baldwin 先生并未受理此事，原因是难以获得运往上海所需的海关护照，同时也考虑到这些装满弹药的箱子在广州可能被用于其他用途。

黄漢忠 (Wong Han Tsong)，别名 H.T. Wong，受雇于广东路3号的美国商务部，担任秘书一职。他是四川人，其在美国商务部的职位使他能够鼓励那些查询商品的华人购买美国制造的产品。Wong 承认，在1926年8月初的一个晚上，他在南京路先施大楼的东方饭店 (Oriental Hotel) 遇到了一位名叫黄季植 (Wong Kwei Chi) 的四川老友，对方问他是否有可能为各种数量的猎枪子弹获取报价。这位朋友刚从四川来，并在那里为广州购买了药品（可能是鸦片）。他打算在前往广州的途中，看看是否有可能在此地为目的地的一位中国体育军火商签订一份合同，该商人将此类子弹出售给那里的商团义勇队，
